claim: Trim/recovery pointers in the R5 §N.6 envelope always name the concrete instrument to call for the rest of a trimmed array ("reference-don't-repeat" discipline).
reality: Multiple live calls return trim_report/drill_pointers entries whose `instrument` field is the literal string "unknown_tool" instead of the actual tool name — the recovery pointer is unusable as written. Observed on ganita_dashas_get (content.rows trimmed 89->44, recover_via.instrument="unknown_tool"), kala_windows_get (content.activations/predicates/signal_id_refs trims, 3x "unknown_tool"), and phala_outlook_get (mitigations/auspicious_windows trims, 2x "unknown_tool").

evidence.quote: trim_report:[{"path":"content.rows","original_count":89,"kept_count":44,..."recover_via":{"instrument":"ganita_dashas_get",...}}] -- NOTE: top-level drill_pointers block for the SAME trim instead read {"instrument":"ganita_dashas_get",...} correctly in this call, but kala_windows_get and phala_outlook_get below show the literal bug

drill_pointers:[{"instrument":"unknown_tool","hint":"call unknown_tool again with a narrower filter/date_range...to reach the rest of \"content.activations\""},{"instrument":"unknown_tool",..."content.predicates\""},{"instrument":"unknown_tool",..."content.signal_id_refs\""}]

drill_pointers:[{"instrument":"unknown_tool","hint":"call unknown_tool again with a narrower filter/date_range...to reach the rest of \"mitigations\""},{"instrument":"unknown_tool",..."auspicious_windows\"}]

recommended_action: Trace the trim_report/drill_pointers generator (shared response_budget.ts helper) — it appears to resolve the calling tool's own name for the self-pointer in some code paths (ganita_dashas_get) but falls back to a hardcoded/unbound "unknown_tool" placeholder in others (kala_windows_get, phala_outlook_get). Likely a tool-name-threading bug in the trim-report constructor for the L3/L4 sidecar-backed tools specifically (both affected tools are alias/sidecar-style, unlike the L1 EAV tools which resolved correctly).

claim: phala_anchors_get's JSON schema declares date_range as an optional object parameter (not in `required`), implying the tool works with chart_id alone.
reality: Calling phala_anchors_get with only chart_id (no date_range) returns a hard error: the underlying sidecar route /api/compute/phala/event_anchors 422s with "Field required" for body.date_range. The MCP-facing schema over-promises: date_range is optional in the tool's own JSON schema but mandatory at the sidecar HTTP layer one hop downstream, and the alias wrapper does not supply a default before forwarding.

evidence.quote: request={chart_id:"482012f1-710e-4a25-994a-93821f5871aa"} (no date_range) -> response: {"ok":false,"error":"Error: [alias] sidecar /api/compute/phala/event_anchors failed (422): {\"detail\":[{\"type\":\"missing\",\"loc\":[\"body\",\"date_range\"],\"msg\":\"Field required\",...}]}","tool":"phala_anchors_get"}

recommended_action: Either mark date_range required in the phala_anchors_get JSON schema, or have the alias wrapper synthesize a sane default date_range (e.g. now..+12mo, matching phala_outlook_get's own default window) before forwarding to the sidecar, so an honest optional-param contract is kept.

claim: ref_dignity_reference_get's `planet` filter is a supported, documented facet ("Filter by planet name... matched case-insensitively against the structured bg_dignity_reference table").
reality: Calling ref_dignity_reference_get with planet="Saturn" (the exact documented usage) returns a hard internal_error, not data: "platform DB query failed: 400". This is a genuinely broken code path on a documented, non-exotic parameter — not a rare edge case.

evidence.quote: request={planet:"Saturn"} -> response: {"ok":false,"error":{"class":"internal_error","message":"Error: [p1_reference] platform DB query failed: 400"},"tool":"ref_dignity_reference_get"}

recommended_action: Reproduce with the exact query the p1_reference layer builds for planet=Saturn against bg_dignity_reference; the 400 from the platform DB layer suggests a malformed query (bad column name / bad param binding) rather than a data-absence case. Fix or, at minimum, catch and translate into an honest empty_reason instead of a 500-class internal_error surfaced to the caller.

claim: BIND_PG-1 assumption A2 (chart_agnostic_gate): every per-chart tool call requires an explicit, real chart_id and must not silently fall back to a default/leaked chart when passed a sentinel or non-existent UUID.
reality: Confirmed for the 3 tools tested. query_chart_facts, get_signals, and ganita_positions_get were each called with the two RFC-sentinel UUIDs the tools' own JSON-schema patterns explicitly permit (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 and ffffffff-ffff-ffff-ffff-ffffffffffff). All three returned clean, honestly-empty results (zero rows, zero facts, empty entity_profiles) scoped to that literal chart_id — no data from chart 482012f1... or any other real chart leaked into the response. The gate holds for this sample.

evidence.quote: chart_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" -> {"signals":[],"returned_count":0,"total_matching_filters":0}, defect_001 status="NO_DATA"
chart_id="ffffffff-ffff-ffff-ffff-ffffffffffff" -> {"rows":[],"total":0}

recommended_action: No action required from this sample; a broader A2 sweep (all ~200 tools, plus a genuinely random non-existent UUID rather than the two schema-whitelisted sentinels) is recommended before fully retiring A2 as closed, since only 3/~200 tools and 2 special-cased UUID values were exercised.

claim: A2 also implies testing the true chart-agnostic case: a tool call that omits chart_id entirely.
reality: Every one of the ~35 tools exercised in this lane declares chart_id as a JSON-schema `required` field with a strict UUID-pattern regex. The MCP client harness itself refuses to construct a call missing a required parameter, so the "omit chart_id" scenario A2 originally frames cannot be exercised from this seat at all — the schema is the enforcement point, before any server-side code runs. This is a genuine gap in what this lane could observe, not evidence the gate is absent.
recommended_action: To close this half of A2, a future lane needs either (a) raw HTTP access to the underlying sidecar/API bypassing the MCP schema layer, or (b) a code read of the route handlers to confirm chart_id is also enforced server-side (defense in depth) and not just client-side by the tool schema.

claim: BIND_PG-1 A1 / RETRIEVAL_STRATEGY's "reference-don't-repeat" drill_pointer premise: a drill_pointer served in one tool's envelope, when followed, actually returns the promised cross-verified detail rather than a dead end.
reality: Confirmed for the one pointer tested end-to-end. ganita_yogas_get's response carries a drill_pointer {instrument:"ganita_yoga_firings_get", hint:"firings-authoritative source...cross-check before asserting fired/not-fired"}. Calling ganita_yoga_firings_get for the same chart returned real, richer data: 12 fired yogas with per-yoga strength scores, bhaṅga/cancellation ledgers (including a full neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga grounds_jsonb rule-by-rule breakdown), versus the origin tool's own thinner catalog view (7 yoga_label rows, 3 flagged catalog_only). The pointer is not decorative — it resolves to substantively different, higher-fidelity data.

evidence.quote: drill_pointers:[{"instrument":"ganita_yoga_firings_get","hint":"firings-authoritative source (ga_yoga_firings): per-yoga strength, bhaṅga/cancellation state, partial-formation %, dāśā-activation windows — cross-check before asserting fired/not-fired (A3/CR-92, R-3)."}]

fired_count implied by response: 12 rows returned incl. neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga with bhanga_active=true and a full grounds_jsonb rule ledger (nbry_rule_1_dispositor_kendra, nbry_rule_2_exaltation_lord_kendra, ...) — data ganita_yogas_get's own page does not carry

recommended_action: None — positive finding. Recommend a wider sample of drill_pointer resolutions (5-10 more pairs) in a follow-up lane to build confidence this holds generally, not just for this one well-tested pair.

claim: BIND_PG-1 states only 3 judgment_flags values are documented anywhere in the codebase, implying the real served vocabulary is largely undiscovered.
reality: This lane's ~35-call sample alone surfaced at least 9 distinct judgment_flags string values actually served on live responses, none of which were pre-verified against the "3 documented" claim but all of which are clearly a much richer vocabulary than 3: catalog_only_rows_present, zero_rows_returned, bearing_yogas_no_domain_match, bearing_yogas_corroboration_caveat, notably_absent_not_checked, afflictions_present, response_still_over_12kb_budget_after_full_trim, timing_anchored_forced_false, and (implicitly, as a documented-but-unobserved sibling) catalog_only_note appearing as a related but separate field. Flags are not free-text — each carries a fixed prefix token (before the first ": ") suggesting a real enum-like vocabulary, but observed only where response_format=v3/legacy-with-envelope was requested; default-legacy calls on many tools return judgment_flags:[] even when the same underlying condition (e.g. catalog-only rows) is present in `content`.

evidence.quote: response_format=v3 -> judgment_flags:["catalog_only_rows_present: 3 row(s) in this page are catalog_only/requires_pass label matches (JL-004)..."]
facet=dosha_fires, response_format=v3 -> judgment_flags:["zero_rows_returned"]

domain=marriage, response_format=v3 -> judgment_flags:["bearing_yogas_no_domain_match: ...","bearing_yogas_corroboration_caveat: ...","notably_absent_not_checked: ...","afflictions_present: ...","response_still_over_12kb_budget_after_full_trim","timing_anchored_forced_false: ..."]

recommended_action: Grep the platform-mcp source for every `judgment_flags.push(` / string-literal site to enumerate the true vocabulary exhaustively (this lane's sample is necessarily partial — ~35 of ~200 tools, mostly response_format=legacy which suppresses the field). A dedicated follow-up lane with time budget for a full grep + cross-check against whatever "3 documented" source BIND_PG-1 was citing would close this cleanly.

claim: The R5 §N.6 envelope's coverage/total field is meant to disclose the true family size behind a paginated/trimmed response (so a caller can tell 'this is everything' vs 'this is a slice').
reality: coverage.total is populated (non-null) only when response_format=v3 is explicitly requested and the underlying handler computes a verdict; under the DEFAULT legacy envelope (which the large majority of tools return unless the caller opts in), the top-level `pagination.total` field is frequently null even though a real total clearly exists downstream (e.g. ganita_strength_get: pagination.total=null at the envelope level, but content.total=520 is present one level down in the same response; ganita_condition_get: pagination.total=null, content.total=340; ganita_nakshatra_get: pagination.total=null, content.total=39). The information is not lost, but a caller reading only the promoted envelope pagination block (as the R5 unified-envelope discipline implies they should) gets a false 'total unknown' impression when it is in fact known and sitting in `content`.

evidence.quote: pagination:{"offset":0,"limit":0,"total":null,...} ... content:{...,"total":520}
pagination:{"offset":0,"limit":0,"total":null,...} ... content:{...,"total":340}
response_format=v3 -> pagination:{"offset":0,"limit":500,"total":10,...} AND coverage:{"served":10,"total":10} -- total correctly non-null when v3 requested

recommended_action: Have the shared envelope-construction helper always promote content.total (when present) up to pagination.total/coverage.total regardless of response_format, instead of only doing so on the v3 code path.

claim: Response payloads for whole-chart-read / signal-heavy tools are large enough that the response_budget trimmer is load-bearing, not a rare edge case.
reality: Every ga_structural/ga_condition/ga_sade_sati-class call in this sample triggered the trimmer: ganita_strength_get 520->65 rows, ganita_condition_get(karakas) 340->85 rows, ganita_sade_sati_get 1259->78 rows, ganita_dashas_get 89->44 rows. bodha_domain_reading_get's own per-lens caps (25/lens, 200 signal_id_refs of 3107 total) and bodha_chart_digest_get's family-collapse (300 candidates -> 107 family rows -> top_k=20) show the same pattern at the L2 Bodha layer. This is consistent with the D-1.5b Serving Density Principle (CLAUDE.md §N.6) working as designed, not a defect — recorded as a confirmed density-contract observation for the retrieval-plane audit.

evidence.quote: trim_report:[{"path":"rows","original_count":520,"kept_count":65,...}]
trim_report:[{"path":"rows","original_count":1259,"kept_count":78,...}]

lens all_relevant_ranked_jsonb.total_count=3134 (career lens) / 5599 (progeny lens); served ranked_signals capped at 5/lens post-trim; signal_id_refs_total=3107, signal_id_refs_capped=true (200 served)

recommended_action: None — working as designed; flagged for the retrieval-plane elevation plan as evidence the density contract is genuinely load-bearing at scale, useful context for future budget-sizing decisions.

claim: All ~200 MCP tools return a consistent top-level envelope shape (the R5 unified envelope or a simple {type,object:{content:...}} wrapper) that a generic caller can parse uniformly.
reality: mimamsa_calibration_get and mimamsa_insight_get (and phala_mitigation_get) break the pattern: their `result.results[0].content` field is itself a JSON-encoded STRING (not a nested object) that must be parsed a second time to reach the actual data — e.g. mimamsa_calibration_get's real qa_results/multipliers/qa_summary payload (141 QA checks) is embedded as an escaped JSON string inside results[0].content, wrapped inside a tool_bundle_id/KEYSTONE-style envelope distinct from every other tool sampled in this lane. A caller written against the common envelope shape will silently get a raw string instead of structured data from these three tools.

evidence.quote: result.results[0].content = "{\"chart_id\":\"482012f1-...\",\"verdict_distribution\":[],\"reliability_curve\":[],\"multipliers\":[...]}"  -- a JSON string, not an object, one level deeper than every other tool's content field

result.results[0].content = "{\"chart_id\":\"482012f1-...\",\"remedies\":[{\"mitigation_id\":...}]…[truncated for budget]"  -- same double-encoding pattern, also truncated mid-JSON by the response budget which risks an unparseable fragment

affects: registration path / sidecar consistency (R-1's KEYSTONE REQUEST sidecar finding)
recommended_action: These three tools are almost certainly the "three live KEYSTONE REQUEST sidecar tools" R-1 flagged in server.ts comments as the concrete A4 sidecar pull-in inventory — confirms via independent observation that the sidecar-backed tools carry a genuinely different wire shape than registry-backed tools. Recommend either normalizing the envelope (parse server-side before returning) or explicitly documenting the double-encoding in each tool's description so callers know to double-parse.
